Rashi on Sotah 22b:1:1.english: And until how much [age] - Is he considered fit for [issuing] halakhic rulings?

Rashi on Sotah 22b:1:2.hebrew: והא רבה אורי - וכל שנותיו אינן אלא מ', כדאמרי' בר"ה (דף יח.): רבה ואביי מדבית עלי קאתו כו':
Rashi on Sotah 22b:1:2.english: But Rabbah tormented [others] - And all his years were only forty, as we say in Rosh Hashanah (18a): Rabbah and Abaye came from the house of Eli, etc.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:1:3.hebrew: בשוין - אם שוה לגדול העיר בחכמה, מותר להורות; או שאין זקן ממנו בעיר:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:1:3.english: When they are equal - If he is equal to the greatest of the city in wisdom, it is permitted [for him] to rule; or [if] there is no one older than him in the city.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:2:1.hebrew: פרוש שיכמי, פרוש נקפי, פרוש קיזאי, פרוש מדוכיא - כולהו מפרש להו:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:2:1.english: A Shikhmi Pharisee, a Nikpi Pharisee, a Kizai Pharisee, a Medukhya Pharisee - He explains all of them.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:3:1.hebrew: מעשה שכם - שמלו שלא לשם שמים, אף זה מעשיו להנאתו, שיכבדוהו בני אדם ולא לשם שמים:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:3:1.english: The act of Shechem - For [the people of Shechem] circumcised themselves not for the sake of Heaven. So too this one does his deeds for his own benefit, so that people will honor him, and not for the sake of Heaven.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:3:2.hebrew: המנקיף רגליו - מהלך בשפלות, עקב בצד גודל, ואינו מרים רגליו מן הארץ, ומתוך כך מנקף אצבעותיו באבנים:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:3:2.english: One who strikes his feet - He walks in lowliness, heel beside big toe, and does not lift his feet from the ground, and as a result he strikes his toes against stones.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:3:3.hebrew: מקיז דם לכתלים - עושה עצמו כעוצם עיניו שלא יסתכל בנשים, ומתוך כך מכה ראשו בכותל, והדם יוצא:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:3:3.english: One who sheds blood on the walls - He behaves like one who shuts his eyes so as not to look at women, and as a result he strikes his head against the wall, and blood comes out.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:3:4.english: Who is a "mishpa'" - One who walks bent over.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:3:5.hebrew: כי מדוכיא - בוכנא, עשוי כמקבת, וראשו כפוף:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:3:5.english: Like a pestle - A pestle [is] made like a hammer, and its head is bent.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:4:1.hebrew: פרוש מה חובתי ואעשנה - למדוני מה עלי לעשות, ואעשה:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:4:1.english: A Parush [who says], "What is my obligation, that I may perform it?" - Teach me what I must do, and I will do it.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:4:2.hebrew: הא מעליותא היא - אם אינו בקי באיסורין ודקדוקי מצות, ובא ללמוד:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:4:2.english: But this is praiseworthy! - [This applies] if he is not well-versed in the prohibitions and the fine details of the commandments, and he comes to learn.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:4:3.hebrew: מה חובתי תו ואעשנה - מה לעשות עוד ולא עשיתי? ומראה עצמו כאילו קיים את הכל:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:4:3.english: "What is my duty, that I may do it" - What more is there to do that I have not done? And he presents himself as though he has fulfilled everything.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:5:1.hebrew: פרוש מאהבה - מאהבת שכר המצות, ולא לאהבת מצות הבורא:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:5:1.english: A Perush out of love - Out of love for the reward of the commandments, and not out of love for the commandments of the Creator.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:5:2.hebrew: מיראה - של עונשין. אלא מה על האדם לעשות מאהבת הש"י, כאשר צוונו ה' אלהינו, וסוף השכר לבא:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:5:2.english: Out of fear - Of punishments. But [the one who acts out of love does] what a person ought to do out of love of the Holy One, blessed be He, as the Lord our God commanded us, and the ultimate reward is yet to come.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:6:1.hebrew: דמטמרא מטמרא כו' - הנסתרות — נסתרות מבני אדם, והגלויות — גלויות. ומ"מ לב"ד הגדול כולם גלויות, והוא יפרע מן המתכסים בטליתות ומראין עצמן כפרושין, ואינן פרושין:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:6:1.english: That which is concealed is concealed, etc. - The concealed [matters] are concealed from people, and the revealed [matters] are revealed. But nevertheless, to the Great Court [of Heaven] all of them are revealed, and it will exact punishment from those who wrap themselves in prayer shawls and present themselves as Perushim, when they are not [truly] Perushim.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:6:2.hebrew: אל תתיראי מן הפרושין - שהפרושין היו שונאין אותו, לפי שהרג מן החכמים הרבה ונהפך להיות צדוקי, כדאמר בקידושין (דף סו.). וכשמת, היתה אשתו יראה מהן שלא יעבירו המלוכה מבניה, והיתה אומרת לו לבקש מלפניהם עליה. ואמר לה: אל תתיראי מן הפרושין, שצדיקים הן, ולא יגמלוך רעה, ולא לבניך, שלא חטאו להם:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:6:2.english: Do not fear the Perushim - For the Perushim hated him, because he had killed many of the Sages and had turned into a Sadducee, as stated in Kiddushin (66a). And when he was dying, his wife was afraid of them, [fearing] that they would remove the kingship from her sons, and she was telling him to plead before them on her behalf. And he said to her: "Do not fear the Perushim, for they are righteous, and they will not repay evil — neither to you nor to your sons, who did not sin against them."

Rashi on Sotah 22b:6:3.hebrew: ולא ממי שאינן פרושין - שהם אוהביי:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:6:3.english: And not from those who are not Perushim - For they are my friends.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:6:4.hebrew: אלא מן הצבועים - כלומר, שאין מראיתם כתולדותם, אלא צבועין מבחוץ, ואין תוכן כברם:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:6:4.english: Rather, from the dyed ones - That is, their appearance is not like their nature; rather, they are dyed on the outside, and their inside is not like their outside.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:6:5.hebrew: שמעשיהם כמעשה זמרי - שהן רשעים ומבקשים שכר כפנחס, אומרים לבריות לכבדן כפנחס. ואיכא דמפרש לה לענין צניעותא:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:6:5.english: Whose deeds are like the deeds of Zimri - For they are wicked, yet they seek reward like Pinchas; they tell people to honor them like Pinchas. And there are those who explain it as relating to modesty.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:8:1.hebrew: הרי היא ככל המנחות - שנטמאו עד שלא קדשה בכלי:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:8:1.english: Behold, it is like all [other] meal-offerings - that became impure before it was sanctified in a vessel.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:8:2.hebrew: ותפדה - ותצא לחולין, ומהמעות יקנה אחרת:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:8:2.english: And it shall be redeemed - And it goes out to [become] non-sacred [property], and with the money he will buy another.

Rashi on Sotah 22b:8:3.hebrew: ותשרף - שקדשה קדושת הגוף, ואינה יוצאה עוד לחולין:
Rashi on Sotah 22b:8:3.english: And it is burned - For it has been sanctified with the sanctity of the body [of the offering], and it can no longer go out to [become] non-sacred.

Tosafot on Sotah 22b:1:1.hebrew: ועד כמה עד ארבעין שנין - פי' משנה שהתחיל ללמוד עד ארבעים שנה, ולא משנה שנולד. כדאמרינן בפ"ק דמסכת ע"ז (דף ה:): "ולא נתן ה' לכם לב לדעת עד היום הזה", ש"מ לא קאים איניש אדעתיה דרביה עד ארבעין שנין. וזה היה ממתן תורה עד מ' שנה, שאז התחילו ללמוד:
Tosafot on Sotah 22b:1:1.english: "And until when? Until forty years" - Explanation: [it means] years from when he began to learn, up to forty years, and not years from when he was born. As we say in the first chapter of tractate Avodah Zarah (5b): "But the Lord has not given you a heart to know until this day" (Deuteronomy 29:3) — we learn from this [abbreviated: shema minah] that a person does not fully grasp his teacher's meaning until forty years. And this [period] was from the giving of the Torah until forty years [later], when they began to learn.

Tosafot on Sotah 22b:1:2.english: When they are equal - Rashi explains: if he is equal to the leading sage of the city in wisdom, he is permitted to rule. This is difficult for Rabbi Yitzchak (Ri) from the chapter "HaRo'eh" (Berakhot 63a), where Abaye said: "In a place where there is a man, do not be a man." [The Gemara asks:] Isn't that obvious? [It answers:] It is needed only for [a case where they are] equal. Evidently, where they are equal he should not leap to rule. Therefore it is more reasonable to explain here [as follows]. [The Gemara asks:] But Rabbah ruled, and he had not reached [the age of] ruling, since all his days he lived only forty years! [It answers:] [He ruled] where they were equal. That which [the Gemara] said, that one may not rule until forty years, refers to when he is equal in wisdom to the leading sage of the city, and the leading sage of the city has reached [the age of] ruling. Therefore, since there is a sage there like him who has reached [the age of] ruling in years, while he himself has not reached the years of ruling, he may not rule in his presence. But if he himself is the leading sage of the city in wisdom, then even though he has not reached the required age, he may rule. And Rabbah was the leading sage of the city in wisdom. However, Rabbi Yitzchak (Ri) explained that the passage in the chapter "HaRo'eh" deals with a person who enters a city where there is a sage who rules: there, "do not be a man" applies even when they are equal. But if he is established in the city like him, and equal to him in wisdom, he is permitted to rule, as Rashi explained. And Rabbeinu Chananel explained there: in a place where there is an appointed man who toils over the needs of the community, do not leap into [a position of] authority, even if you are equal. According to this explanation, [the passage in Berakhot] is not dealing with ruling at all.

Tosafot on Sotah 22b:2:1.hebrew: פרוש מאהבה פרוש מיראה - בירושל' פרק הרואה: עשה מאהבה ועשה מיראה. עשה מאהבה — שאם באת לשנוא, דע שאתה אוהבו, ואין אוהב שונא. עשה מיראה — שאם באת לבעוט, דע שאתה ירא, ואין ירא מבעט. שבעה פרושין הן: פרוש שכמי וכו', פרוש מן הנכייה כו'. פרוש שכמי — טעון מצותיה על כתפיה. פרוש נקפי — אקיף לי ואני עבד מצוה. פרוש קיזאי — עבד חדא חובה וחדא מצוה, ומקיז חדא בחדא. פרוש מן הנכייה — מאי דאית לי אנא מנכה ועבד מצות. פרוש אדע חובתי ואעשנה — הי דא חובתי עבדית דאעביד מצות דכותה. פרוש יראה — כאיוב. פרוש אהבה — כאברהם, דכתיב (ישעיהו מ״א:ח׳): "זרע אברהם אוהבי". אין לך חביב מכולם אלא פרוש אהבה כאברהם:
Tosafot on Sotah 22b:2:1.english: A Pharisee out of love, a Pharisee out of fear - In the Yerushalmi, chapter "HaRo'eh": Act out of love and act out of fear. Act out of love — for if you come to hate [Him], know that you love Him, and one who loves does not hate. Act out of fear — for if you come to rebel, know that you fear [Him], and one who fears does not rebel. "There are seven [types of] Pharisees: the Shikhmi Pharisee, etc., the Pharisee who discounts, etc." The Shikhmi Pharisee — carries his commandments on his shoulder. The "Nakfi" Pharisee — [he says:] "Let me knock [i.e., wait], and I will perform a commandment." The "Kizai" Pharisee — performs one obligation and one commandment, and offsets [lit., bleeds] one against the other. The Pharisee who discounts — "Whatever I have, I discount [from my debt], and I perform commandments." The Pharisee [who says] "Let me know my obligation and I will do it" — "Which obligation of mine have I performed, that I may perform a commandment like it?" The Pharisee of fear — like Job. The Pharisee of love — like Abraham, as it is written (Isaiah 41:8): "The seed of Abraham, who loved Me." There is none more beloved than all of them except the Pharisee of love, like Abraham.

Tosafot on Sotah 22b:5:1.hebrew: לעולם יעסוק אדם בתורה ובמצות אע"פ שלא לשמה - ואי קשיא, הא אמרינן בפ"ק דתענית (דף ז.): כל העוסק בתורה שלא לשמה — נעשית לו סם המות; ובשלהי פרק היה קורא במסכת ברכות (דף יז.): כל העוסק בתורה שלא לשמה — נוח לו שלא נברא. נראה לתרץ: עוסק שלא לשמה כגון מיראת היסורין, כי הכא, ומאהבת קיבול פרס — שאינו מתכוין להשלים רצון יוצרו שציוהו על כך, אלא להנאתו, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דמסכת ע"ז (דף יט.): "במצותיו חפץ מאד" — ולא בשכר מצותיו. והיינו דתנן (אבות פ"א מ"ג): "אל תהיו כעבדים המשמשין את הרב ע"מ לקבל פרס". וכי הא דאמר בפ' עגלה ערופה (לקמן סוטה מז.), ואיתא בנזיר פרק מי שאמר הריני נזיר (דף כג:) ובפרק בתרא דהוריות (דף י:): "לעולם יעסוק אדם וכו'", שבשכר מ"ב קרבנות שהקריב בלק זכה ויצאה ממנו רות. גם הוא נתכוין להנאתו, שהעלה קרבן לשם להשלים חפציו בשכרו, ולא לשם שמים; וכדאמרי' פ"ק דר"ה (דף ד.): "האומר סלע זו לצדקה ע"מ שיחיה בני — ה"ז צדיק גמור". אבל ההיא שלא לשמה דתענית ומס' ברכות — אינו עוסק בתורה כדי לקיים, לא מאהבה ולא מיראה, אלא להוסיף על חטאתו פשע, שעתה שגגות נעשו לו זדונות, שאע"פ שידע שעובר לא מנע מכל תאות לבו; כדמפרש התם (ברכות יז.): "תכלית חכמה — תשובה ומעשים טובים, שלא יהא אדם קורא ושונה ומשמש תלמידי חכמים ובועט באביו ובאמו וברבו או במי שגדול הימנו, שנאמר: 'ראשית חכמה יראת ה'.' שכל טוב לכל עושיהם — ללומדיהם לא נאמר, אלא לעושיהם; לעושים לשמה":
Tosafot on Sotah 22b:5:1.english: "A person should always engage in Torah and commandments, even if not for their own sake" - And if one asks: Surely we say in the first chapter of Ta'anit (7a): Anyone who engages in Torah not for its own sake, it becomes for him a potion of death; and at the end of the chapter "Hayah Korei" in tractate Berakhot (17a): Anyone who engages in Torah not for its own sake, it would have been better for him had he not been created. It appears to resolve [this]: One who engages [in Torah] "not for its own sake" [in the sense permitted here] is, for example, [one who does so] out of fear of suffering, as here, or out of love of receiving a reward — [meaning] that he does not intend to fulfill the will of his Creator, Who commanded him about this, but rather [acts] for his own benefit, as we say in the first chapter of tractate Avodah Zarah (19a): "In His commandments he delights greatly" — and not in the reward of His commandments. And this is what we learned (Avot 1:3): "Do not be like servants who serve the master on condition of receiving a reward." And so it is [in the case of] what was said in the chapter "Eglah Arufah" (below, Sotah 47a), and it appears in Nazir, in the chapter "Mi She'amar Harei Ani Nazir" (23b), and in the last chapter of Horayot (10b): "A person should always engage, etc.," for in reward for the forty-two offerings that Balak offered, he merited that Ruth descended from him. He too intended his own benefit, since he brought an offering there in order to fulfill his needs through its reward, and not for the sake of Heaven; and as we say in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (4a): One who says, "This sela is for charity on condition that my son will live" — he is a completely righteous person. But that "not for its own sake" of Ta'anit and tractate Berakhot — [that person] does not engage in Torah in order to fulfill [it], neither out of love nor out of fear, but rather to add transgression to his sin, so that now his unintentional sins become for him deliberate ones, for even though he knows that he is transgressing, he does not restrain himself from any desire of his heart; as it is explained there (Berakhot 17a): "The goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, that a person should not read and study and serve Torah scholars and yet rebel against his father and mother and his teacher, or against one who is greater than he, as it is stated: 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord.' 'Good understanding to all who practice them' — it is not said 'to those who study them,' but 'to those who practice them'; to those who practice [it] for its own sake."

Tosafot on Sotah 22b:8:1.hebrew: אלו שמנחותיהם נשרפות - תימה: אמאי לא חשיב נמי מת הוא או שמתה היא, דאמרי' בפ"ק (לעיל סוטה דף ו:) דנשרפת? וליכא למימר דוקא היינו לאחר שקידש הקומץ, כדתני' לעיל. אבל הכא לא חשיב אלא הנשרפת משקדשה בכלי, דה"ה אם משקדשה בכלי דנשרפת. ואיידי דקתני סיפא "קירב הקומץ" דנאכלת, נקט רישא "קידש הקומץ". ורבותא נקט: אע"פ דכבר קדוש וקרוב להקרבה טפי מקידשה בכלי, אפ"ה נשרפת:
Tosafot on Sotah 22b:8:1.english: "These are the ones whose meal-offerings are burned" - It is puzzling: why does it not also count "he died" or "she died," for we said in the first chapter (above, Sotah 6b) that [the meal-offering] is burned? And one cannot say that this applies specifically after the handful was sanctified, as was taught above. But here it counts only the meal-offering that is burned from the time it was sanctified in a vessel, for the same is true if, after it was sanctified in a vessel, it is burned. And since the latter clause teaches "the handful was offered up," in which case [the remainder] is eaten, the first clause takes up "the handful was sanctified." And it states a novelty: even though [the handful] was already sanctified and is closer to being offered than one that was merely sanctified in a vessel, nevertheless it is burned:
